subject: Materials Science
title: Color Centers: Defects You Can See
description: Learn Color Centers: Defects You Can See in one minute.

hook.text: Pure corundum is colorless. Add a trace of chromium and it becomes a blood-red ruby.

buildup.text: Color centers are point defects that trap electrons, absorbing specific light wavelengths.

discovery.text: An F-center is an electron trapped in an anion vacancy — it colors NaCl crystals yellow or purple.

twist.text: Irradiating quartz creates color centers that turn it smoky brown — nature does this underground over millennia.

climax.text: Sapphire's blue comes from iron and titanium impurities — the same mineral as ruby, different defects.

punchline.text: The most beautiful gems owe their color to atomic imperfections.

quiz.question: What causes the color in gemstones like ruby?
options: Point defects and impurity atoms that absorb specific wavelengths
The crystal's overall size and shape
